---
title: Summary (results object)
aliases:
  - attributes.html
---

`model.fit()` returns a `Summary` object. In examples below it is assigned to
`results`. Its everyday attributes are direct,
named `pandas.Series` or scalar values; optimizer implementation details are
kept under `optim_result`.

## Everyday use

| Attribute | Description |
|---|---|
| `params` | Estimated coefficients indexed by variable name. |
| `bse` | Conventional standard errors indexed like `params`. |
| `robust_bse` | Robust sandwich standard errors indexed like `params`. |
| `bse_at(params, robust=False)` | Standard errors evaluated at supplied parameter values. `False` (default) omits robust adjustments; `True` uses the configured robust covariance. Does not optimize. |
| `bse_at_diagnostics(params)` | Both SE variants plus score, Hessian conditioning, weakest scaled-Hessian direction, and variance clipping diagnostics at supplied values. |
| `tvalues` | Test statistics based on robust standard errors. |
| `pvalues` | Two-sided p-values based on robust standard errors. |
| `conf_int(alpha=0.05)` | Two-sided confidence intervals based on robust standard errors. |
| `nobs` | Number of observations used in the fit. |
| `df_resid` | Residual degrees of freedom. |
| `llf` | Maximized log-likelihood. |
| `aic`, `bic` | Information criteria. |
| `converged` | Whether optimization converged. |
| `random_effects` | Object exposing `.group` and `.time` residual effects and standard deviations. |
| `resid` | Regression residuals. |
| `fittedvalues` | Fitted dependent-variable values. |
| `forecast(steps=1)` | Future dependent-variable values for each panel unit. |
| `summary()` | Formats a human-readable regression summary. |

```{python}
#| eval: false
results.params
results.bse
results.robust_bse
results.summary()
```

`bse_at()` accepts a complete `dict` or `pandas.Series` keyed by the same
parameter names as `results.params`. It evaluates the likelihood, gradient,
and Hessian at those values without re-estimating the model. By default,
`robust=False` returns standard errors without HAC or cluster adjustments.
Set `robust=True` to use paneltime's configured robust covariance, including
its default Newey-West lag and panel-cluster adjustments. Built-in likelihoods
use analytic derivatives; custom likelihoods may use the finite-difference
fallback. This is useful in simulations where the true coefficients are known.
The returned standard errors remain sample-specific; they are not theoretical
or Monte Carlo standard errors.

For example, start with a complete fitted-parameter vector and replace values
whose simulation truths are known:

```{python}
#| eval: false
true_params = results.params.copy()
true_params["X0"] = 1.0
true_params["X1"] = 1.0
se_at_truth = results.bse_at(true_params)
```

The current initial variance and random-effect variance components are not
free entries in `params`; they remain determined by the fitted model/data.
`conf_int(alpha=...)` uses the requested significance level, where `alpha`
must be between zero and one.
Forecast requests must fit within the future prediction rows prepared by the
model; unavailable horizons raise `ValueError` instead of returning a partial
panel slice.

`bse_at_diagnostics()` accepts the same complete parameter mapping and returns
both `bse` and `robust_bse`, the log-likelihood, total and per-observation
scores, Hessian diagonal, raw Hessian condition number, scaled condition index,
weakest direction of the diagonally scaled Hessian, and fraction of included
conditional variances clipped at model bounds. The scaled condition index is
the eigenvalue-ratio diagnostic used by paneltime's multicollinearity report.

## Optimizer internals (advanced)

Advanced diagnostics are available from `results.optim_result`, including
`hessian`, `gradient_matrix`, `gradient_vector`, `dx_norm`, `its`, `msg`,
`t0`, `t1`, and `log_likelihood_object`.

For compatibility, `results.output` and `results.table` expose engine objects.
Prefer the direct result attributes above for routine analysis; the engine
objects are implementation details.
